messages:
Priya: Heads up — Sunburst (early stage fintech) wants a 2-week trial. They expect ~50 req/s peak, avg prompt ~900 tokens, plus a rerank step. Can we confirm which catalog models/variants support long KV cache and q4 quant without large perf regressions? Also they asked for a commit estimate for reserved capacity pricing. @Sofia can you take infra perf + autoscale checks?
Sofia: noted. Is the 900 tokens including history or per-turn? that changes mem footprint. :thinking:
Priya: per-turn (they keep short system + 2-3 turns). rerank prompts are ~300 tokens.
Diego: For q4 quant we should check memory headroom. I can run quick perf on gigante-2-16k and sprig-8k variants. If they need long-kv for 900 tokens plus 8k context for embeddings, we might need a variant with kv-snapshot enabled.
Alex: FYI legal flagged SOC2 + data residency. They want an answer on how long ephemeral caches live and whether we persist request logs from trial.
Mariam: We typically set ephemeral KV cache TTL to session lifetime and we don't persist KV by default. For trials we should offer no-logging mode (audit: no request logging) — need to check with infra if that impacts tracing/alerting.
Sofia: I can validate autoscale profile. Quick note: at 50 req/s with batching turned on, we should hit sub-100ms p50 with gigante-2-16k-q4 on our Dedicated pool, but p95 will depend on burst capacity. Need to confirm burst windows.
Priya: Great. Also pricing ask: they want a 1-month reserved dev pool estimate with burst allowance. Any rough numbers?
Alex: For dev reserved monthly, baseline is $Xk for a small pool (2xA40 equiv) + usage overage. I'll pull exact numbers. We can offer a discounted onboarding credit too.
Diego: Running a quick local run now. Sample command I'm using:
```bash
redwood run --model redwood/gigante-2-16k-q4 --batching auto --kv-cache enable --concurrency 64 --test-requests 2000
```
Diego: Early results: memory okay, but quantized FP16->q4 shows ~8-10% latency bump on long contexts. Will try sprig-8k variant as smaller context alternative.
Priya: Can you also check compatibility with their on-prem connector? They want to keep PII in their VPC and hit our private endpoint.
Mariam: For private deployment we support VPC peering and can disable telemetry. Need Sales to confirm commitment level.
Sofia: Ops question: if they disable logging, can we still trace failures for rollouts? ops-bot: Canary traces will emit perf metrics but request bodies are redacted when logging is disabled.
Priya: Perfect. Diego — ETA for perf matrix?
Diego: I can have a short matrix (3 variants x latency/mem) by EOD PST.
Alex: I'll draft the reserved capacity quote and include onboarding credit.
Priya: Heads up on an enterprise blocker: security questionnaire asked whether model files ever leave our encrypted storage during scaling. Need a concise answer.
Mariam: Short answer: no, model artifacts are pulled from encrypted model registry to nodes over TLS and never stored unencrypted on disk. I'll add exact wording for the questionnaire.
Priya: Thanks. One more: Sunburst asked about model variant pinning — they want deterministic rollout and fallback on a cheaper model if p95 > threshold. Can our routing policy do that?
Sofia: Yes, routing policy supports canary + fallback to a compatible quantized variant by model family tag. We'll need to map "gigante-2" -> "sprig" fallback in the routing config.
Diego: I'll include compatible-variant list in the matrix.
Priya: Awesome. After Diego posts the perf matrix and Alex the quote, I'll assemble a single response for the customer with next steps, runbook for the trial, and legal wording.
Alex: tagging @mariam for the exact SOC2 wording.
Mariam: uploading suggested SOC2 answers in 1h.
ops-bot: Deployment check scheduled: 1715003600. Canary window 30m. Notifying eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
Priya: Thanks everyone. If anything blocks the quote or perf results ping me directly. :pray:
